## 6. Optimization Proposals (all 4 dimensions walked per rule 14)

### Compute (L1/L2)
- **RCCL/nccl distributed backend** (vs. gloo). Citation: Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH," IJHPCA 2005. Expected: faster grad all-reduce. **Status: applied, measured +1.2% (noise) — not credited, though retained as safe default.**
- **DeepSpeed ZeRO stage 1**. Citation: Rajbhandari et al., "ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models," SC 2020. **Status: applied, measured -20.2% — REGRESSION, reverted.**
- **bf16 instead of fp16.** Citation: Kalamkar et al., "A Study of BFLOAT16 for Deep Learning Training," arXiv:1905.12322. **Status: applied, measured ~-25% — REGRESSION, reverted.**
- **TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1/0.** Citation: AMD ROCm hipBLASLt documentation. **Status: applied both directions, -2.0% / -0.6% — inert both ways, confirms dead knob.**
- **FlashAttention.** Citation: Dao et al., "FlashAttention," NeurIPS 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135. Estimated ~17% (highest-ceiling untested lever). **Status: NOT measured — flash_attn absent, DeepSpeed 0.19.3 FlashAttentionBuilder returns None, Megatron silently falls back to use_flash_attn=False. Needs a multi-hour ROCm/CK build; deferred.**

### I/O (full checklist, all "not applicable")
- All 12 checklist items walked and marked **not applicable**: steady-state training issues zero POSIX ops; the only I/O (10.2 GB) occurs in iteration 1 and iterations 2-3 run entirely from page cache.
- **num_workers=0**: applicable candidate, value purely a production-scale argument. **Status: applicable, NOT measured at this scale.**

### Memory (L1/L2/L3)
- **ZeRO-1 optimizer-state partitioning** (same proposal as Compute) — optimizer-state construction measured at only 2.0% of pretrain span, correctly predicting no capacity pressure to relieve on MI300A's unified HBM. **Status: applied, measured, regression, confirms the memory-dimension prediction.**
- Checkpoint memory/I-O: **not applicable/unmeasured** — zero checkpoints written (save-interval 10 > 3 train iterations).

### Communication (L1/L2/L3)
- **RCCL/nccl backend** — **Status: applied, measured +1.2%, NO CHANGE within noise** (session's most counter-intuitive result, see finding #1).
- Gradient-accumulation-fusion/overlap tuning: not separately tested; grad-accum=4 over 16 ranks already keeps all-reduce a small fraction of iteration time per the RCCL-swap result.

## 7. Optimization Ledger

| # | Dimension | Level | Change | Applied? | Measured delta | Significance/replicates | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | communication | L2 | gloo -> nccl (RCCL) distributed backend | yes | +1.2% (147.1 vs 145.4 sps) | 1 replicate | harmless-but-not-credited (within noise; adopt as safe default) |

| 7 | io | L1-L3 (12-item checklist) | (all 12 strategies) | no | not measured (steady-state I/O = 0 ops) | n/a | not-applicable — structurally absent bottleneck |
| 8 | io | L1 | num_workers>0 / prefetch_factor | no (scale-gated) | not measured | n/a | applicable-not-measured — needs production-scale dataset |
| 9 | memory | n/a | checkpoint I/O tuning | no | not measured (zero checkpoints written) | n/a | not-applicable this session, unmeasured |

**Mechanism paragraphs:**

- **Row 1 (RCCL swap, +1.2% vs ~35% trace-derived estimate):** At 350M params with global_batch 256 / micro_batch 4 (grad-accum 4) across 16 ranks, the gradient all-reduce payload is small relative to per-rank compute time (~1.76s/step). A trace-derived estimate assuming proportional communication cost predicted ~35% improvement; measured effect was ~30x smaller — a clear demonstration that a plausible trace-derived projection can be badly wrong when compute/communication overlap is already present. Measure, don't extrapolate.
- **Row 2/3 (ZeRO-1 and bf16 regressions):** Both target relieving pressure that doesn't exist at this scale on MI300A's unified HBM — optimizer-state construction is only 2.0% of pretrain time, so partitioning it adds coordination overhead without removing a real constraint; bf16's regression is consistent with apex's fused kernels already being fp16-tuned (finding #2), losing a well-optimized fast path rather than gaining one.
- **Row 5 (hipBLASLt env var, inert both directions):** Regresses in BOTH "on" and "off" (control) positions relative to baseline, by amounts smaller than cross-replicate noise — not a real lever on this stack; treat as absent from the tuning surface.

## 9. Lessons Learned

- New lessons persisted this session (see git-tracked memory under `src/dftracer_agents/.agents/workspace/memory/`, listed in Finalization): Cray `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` ordering for Fortran runtime, `@dft.log`/`@classmethod` decorator ordering, mpi4py Cray soname mismatch, Tuolumne ROCm torch wheel requirement, Tuolumne `ROCM_HOME` auto-detection gap for DeepSpeed op-builder, Megatron-DeepSpeed JIT/lock pitfalls, launcher world-size-1 trap, smoke-test data-slicing, ROCm apex/run pitfalls, torchvision ABI mismatch.
- Pitfall discovered and corrected mid-session: a false premise that ROCm apex produced only a Python fallback (no fused HIP kernels), based on misreading DeepSpeed's op-builder table. Corrected by direct import probe (finding #2); preserved in the report rather than silently dropped.
- No new MCP tool changes were required; findings were produced via existing `analyze`/`diagnose`/`comparator` tools plus targeted manual trace-event breakdowns where the tool's aggregate summary didn't separate import-storm STDIO from application STDIO.

## 10. Recommendations for Future Runs

- **What worked well:** the 4-node/16-rank baseline, once genuinely distributed (attempt 10), gave a clean, reproducible 2-iteration steady-state signal; the full 4-dimension optimizer dispatch surfaced the counter-intuitive RCCL finding a narrower optimizer would likely have missed.
- **What needs improvement:** (1) bracket every run with `dftracer_service` node-counter start/stop per rule 12 — this session did not, and the memory dimension had zero HBM/occupancy data as a result; (2) avoid launching competing jobs on shared allocations — two of this session's own launches collided with the compute agent's replicate study, silently SIGABRT-killing one bf16 replicate.
- **Known limitations:** all findings scoped to a 4000-doc pre-sliced dataset at 3-20 iterations; I/O-negligibility and dataloader-stall conclusions do not generalize to production-scale corpora or longer runs; FlashAttention remains the highest-ceiling untested lever pending a ROCm/CK build.
